answer: Make every identity carry an unforgeable pigment. The tag derives from host boot counters and when its first answer was sealed, so two keys opened on one machine diverge within a round. A falcon patrol samples sealed tags and replays each against its own drift record; a match byte for byte means a copy, and a copy forfeits its deposit. Clones then sit in a glacier of frozen rewards: the more aliases stacked on one host, the longer the shared tag waits to be sampled, so the pile stays locked while it keeps paying authoring cost.
